title: ticfac Phase 5: actually drive a run from the Cloudflare host
description:
Phase 4 built the components. Nothing drives them.

Its final review (pxc, 2026-09-19) established that the Phase 4 gate cannot be performed as things stand, and the reasons compound:

- EpicReconcilerWorkflow is bound in wrangler.toml but NOTHING under cloudflare/src calls EPIC_RECONCILER.create. runs.ts still starts RUN_WORKFLOW, which boots a container agent. No deployed run is driven by the new reconciler.
- The Workflow reconciler never persists the sandbox handle, so every later pass and every restart inspects with undefined. No real attempt can be re-inspected — the durable-evidence doctrine the whole design rests on is absent on the cloud host. FakeExecutor keys on job_id, which is why no test caught it.
- There is no CI-gated close-out and no PR-posted review on the Workflow host. The Go admitCloseout has no TypeScript counterpart, so the gated hand-over cannot happen there.

So Phase 4 delivered the move, the reconciler, run records out of D1, the serialized publisher and the sandbox executor — and did not deliver a run driven by any of them. Phase 5 is that, and nothing wider.

This epic also carries the concurrency and contract defects the review found in the same code, because they are the reason a real run would not survive: sibling token revocation under max_parallel > 1, attempt records that do not match the job_handle contract, and a re-acquired publish slot token that is not used for its own pass's writes.

Definition of done is deliberately one sentence with no room to argue: an epic runs to completion driven by EpicReconcilerWorkflow on a deployed Factory, its attempts survive a restart of the Workflow, and it hands over a reviewed, CI-verified PR.
acceptance_criteria: A real epic completes on a deployed Cloudflare Factory driven by EpicReconcilerWorkflow; at least one attempt is adopted by identity after a Workflow restart; the close-out gates on CI and opens a PR carrying the review's verdict and findings; max_parallel > 1 runs without a worker losing its gateway token
